class.name: HTMLView
class.brief_description: Control that draws a pure HTML/CSS document as a texture.
class.description: Draws an [HTMLDocument] into the control rectangle. Actions are delivered through Godot signals and bound [Callable]s. Resizing the control updates the HTML viewport while keeping the current document state alive.

members.member: Preferred render backend. [constant BACKEND_AUTO] prefers a GPU target backend on supported D3D12/Vulkan renderers and falls back to the CPU/raw output path with a warning when no GPU target is available. Explicit GPU values report unsupported when the required native target handoff is unavailable and do not fall back to CPU output.

If [code]true[/code], supported simple CSS [code]backdrop-filter[/code] regions are composited by Godot using the screen backbuffer behind this control. The initial supported path handles blur and is prepared for ordered color-filter operations reported by the renderer. Unsupported backdrop regions remain available through [method get_backdrop_filter_regions] but are not drawn by this MVP path.
Convenience access to the assigned document's inline CSS source.
Convenience access to the assigned document's ordered CSS file list.
Document rendered by this view.
If [code]true[/code], the view grabs keyboard focus when clicked.

Optional end-to-end budget from an HTML frame request until its synchronized output group is activated. A positive value enables [signal frame_budget_missed]; [code]0.0[/code] disables reporting. Exceeding this budget never permits dropping animation samples, substituting stale pixels, or activating different generations across outputs.
Godot input action translated to Enter for focused HTML activation.
Godot input action translated to Tab.
Godot input action translated to Shift+Tab.
Convenience access to the assigned document's inline HTML source.
Convenience access to the assigned document's HTML file path.
If [code]true[/code], the view accepts pointer, wheel, key, text, and mapped action input for HTML interaction.

Explicit CSS layout and input coordinate size shared by the automatic Control presentation and every secondary [HTMLViewOutput]. [code]Vector2i(0, 0)[/code] keeps the viewport-mode-derived size. Changing this value performs one shared layout; it does not create independent document state per output.
HTML viewport size used when [member viewport_size_mode] is [constant VIEWPORT_SIZE_FIXED]. If either component is [code]0[/code], the assigned document's default size is used.

Physical raster scale used with [constant VIEWPORT_SIZE_FIXED] without changing its logical CSS viewport. A value of [code]0.0[/code] uses a 1× raster so [member fixed_viewport_size] is the exact render resolution. Set a positive value to request a particular HiDPI or supersampling density.
Godot input action translated to Backspace.
Godot input action translated to Delete.
Godot input action translated to Enter for text submit.
If [code]true[/code], the assigned document's default size is reported as this control's minimum size. Leave disabled when the HTML viewport should follow the actual Control or screen-pixel size.

Controls the logical CSS viewport and physical raster resolution. [constant VIEWPORT_SIZE_FIXED] uses [member fixed_viewport_size] for both unless an explicit [member fixed_viewport_device_scale_factor] requests a denser raster. [constant VIEWPORT_SIZE_CONTROL] uses the Control's local size for both. [constant VIEWPORT_SIZE_CONTROL_PHYSICAL_ADJUSTED] keeps the Control's local size as the logical CSS viewport, but rasters at the final physical size occupied by the transformed Control. [constant VIEWPORT_SIZE_PHYSICAL_SIZE] uses that final physical size for both CSS layout and rasterization.

signal.name: frame_activated
signal.description: Emitted after the view atomically activates the texture and immutable interaction metadata for this generation. Engine-queue-ordered GPU output activates at submission; producer completion remains asynchronous retirement authority.

signal.name: frame_queued
signal.description: Emitted after a logical frame is submitted to the selected renderer backend.

signal.name: frame_budget_missed
signal.description: Emitted when a requested frame exceeds [member frame_budget_milliseconds]. [param stage] is [code]physical_pool_blocked[/code] when producer capacity delayed the request, [code]prepare_submit[/code] when the frame was already late when queued, [code]activation[/code] when later activation consumed the budget, or [code]no_visual_output[/code] when a request completed without producing new pixels. [param generation] is the synchronized generation that became active, or the unchanged active generation for [code]no_visual_output[/code].

signal.name: action_requested
signal.description: Emitted when the activation layer requests a Godot action.

signal.name: element_clicked
signal.description: Emitted when an HTML element is clicked.

signal.name: element_pointer_event
signal.description: Emitted for actionable element pointer phases. [param phase] is [code]down[/code], [code]up[/code], [code]cancel[/code], [code]leave[/code], or [code]capture_loss[/code]. The payload retains the pressed element metadata and document position, allowing hold interactions to cancel independently from click activation.

signal.name: render_error
signal.description: Emitted when the renderer or action layer reports an error.

method.name: create_output
method.description: Creates a presentation-only output of the shared logical frame at the requested physical raster size. Set [member logical_size] explicitly first. The output shares DOM, CSS layout, animation, scrolling, focus, and interaction state with this view. Input remains in [member logical_size] coordinates. The initial contract requires the output and logical viewport aspect ratios to match. When [param mipmaps] is [code]true[/code], each completed frame is copied to an sRGB, alpha-weighted mip chain suitable for trilinear or anisotropic 3D material sampling. This does not change level-zero dimensions or logical layout.

method.name: cancel_pointer_interaction
method.description: Cancels the active pointer press, emits [signal element_pointer_event] with the [code]cancel[/code] phase, and prevents later click activation for that press.

method.name: add_css_file
method.description: Appends a CSS file path to the assigned document's CSS file list.

method.name: bind_action
method.description: Binds a Godot callable to an HTML action name.

method.name: get_texture
method.description: Returns the current render texture.

method.name: get_generation
method.description: Returns the latest shared frame generation activated by the automatic Control presentation.

method.name: get_last_frame_budget_result
method.description: Returns the latest completed budget observation with [code]generation[/code], [code]elapsed_milliseconds[/code], [code]budget_milliseconds[/code], [code]missed[/code], and [code]stage[/code]. A request that produces no visual generation is still completed and reported with the [code]no_visual_output[/code] stage.

method.name: get_frame_scheduler_diagnostics
method.description: Returns cumulative terminal outcomes for semantic frame requests. Keys are [code]submitted[/code], [code]no_visual_output[/code], [code]superseded_by_newer_revision[/code], [code]physical_pool_blocked[/code], [code]preparation_failed[/code], and [code]submission_failed[/code]. Producer-capacity retries are counted once per requested revision; retirement maintenance is not an outcome and never contributes backpressure.

method.name: get_backdrop_filter_regions
method.description: Returns dictionaries describing CSS backdrop-filter regions reported by the latest frame. Each dictionary contains [code]element_id[/code], [code]bounds[/code], [code]blur_radius_css_px[/code], four border radius fields, [code]opacity[/code], [code]flags[/code], [code]supported[/code], and [code]filter_operations[/code]. Bounds and radii are in logical HTML coordinates. Each filter operation dictionary contains [code]type[/code] and [code]amount[/code].

method.name: get_form_control_state
method.description: Returns the latest state for a form control in the live document, or an empty [Dictionary] when no control with [param id] is available. The dictionary contains [code]element_id[/code], [code]tag_name[/code], [code]value[/code], [code]checked[/code], [code]selected[/code], [code]selected_index[/code], [code]focused[/code], [code]selection_offsets_present[/code], [code]selection_start[/code], and [code]selection_end[/code].

method.name: local_to_html_position
method.description: Converts a local [HTMLView] position to document pixel coordinates in the rendered HTML viewport.

method.name: set_element_attribute
method.description: Sets an attribute on an element in the live rendered document without reloading the document. Returns [constant OK] on success. The no-script profile rejects inline event handlers and [code]javascript:[/code] URL surfaces with a recoverable error.

method.name: remove_element_attribute
method.description: Removes an attribute from an element in the live rendered document without reloading the document.

method.name: set_element_style
method.description: Replaces the element's inline [code]style[/code] attribute in the live rendered document without reloading the document.

method.name: set_element_text
method.description: Replaces the text content of an element in the live rendered document without reloading the document.

method.name: set_element_inner_html
method.description: Replaces the inner HTML of an element in the live rendered document without reloading the document. The no-script profile rejects unsafe fragments such as scripts, inline event handlers, and [code]javascript:[/code] URL surfaces with a recoverable error.

method.name: set_body_inner_html
method.description: Replaces the inner HTML of the live document body without reloading the document. The no-script profile rejects unsafe fragments such as scripts, inline event handlers, and [code]javascript:[/code] URL surfaces with a recoverable error.

method.name: scroll_element_into_view
method.description: Scrolls the nearest element overflow container ([code]auto[/code] or [code]scroll[/code]) of the element with [param id] so the element's block-start edge is aligned with the scrollport start, clamped to the container's maximum scroll offset. Currently [code]start[/code] is the supported block alignment. The document viewport is not scrolled, and the live document is preserved.

method.name: set_form_control_value
method.description: Sets the live value of a text-like form control without reloading the document.

method.name: set_form_control_checked
method.description: Sets the live checked state of a checkbox or radio control.

method.name: focus_element
method.description: Moves live document focus to the element with [param id].

method.name: blur_focused_element
method.description: Blurs the currently focused element in the live document.

method.name: set_text_selection
method.description: Sets the selection or caret range for a text-like form control in the live document.

method.name: replace_stylesheet_text
method.description: Replaces the text of a [code]<style>[/code] element in the live rendered document without reloading the document.

method.name: has_action
method.description: Returns whether an action has a callable binding.

method.name: clear_css_files
method.description: Clears the assigned document's CSS file list.

method.name: unbind_action
method.description: Removes an action binding.

method.name: remove_css_file
method.description: Removes all matching CSS file paths from the assigned document's CSS file list.

constants.constant: Automatically chooses the best available backend. GPU target rendering is preferred on supported D3D12/Vulkan renderers; CPU/raw output is used as a warned fallback.
Uses the portable CPU texture backend.
Requests an available GPU backend explicitly. This mode does not fall back to CPU output.
Requests the Vulkan GPU backend explicitly.
Requests the D3D12 GPU backend explicitly.
Requests the Metal GPU backend explicitly. This requires Godot's Metal rendering driver and an HCSR build with Metal support.
The HTML viewport follows the Control's local size and uses a device scale factor of [code]1.0[/code].

The HTML viewport follows the Control's local size for CSS/layout coordinates and uses the Control's final screen-pixel scale as device scale factor. This keeps layout stable under window stretch while producing a high-resolution texture.
The HTML viewport uses [member fixed_viewport_size], or the document default size when unset, and Godot scales the resulting texture into the Control.

The HTML viewport follows the Control's final physical screen-pixel size and uses a device scale factor of [code]1.0[/code]. This mode is useful when the HTML output itself must resize to the actual window/backbuffer pixel resolution.
Backdrop filter metadata flag indicating a simple rounded-rectangle clip.
Backdrop filter metadata flag indicating that the region has a complex clip unsupported by the current Godot compositor path.
Backdrop filter metadata flag indicating that the region has a transform unsupported by the current Godot compositor path.
Backdrop filter metadata flag indicating that the CSS backdrop filter contains an operation other than the simple blur supported by the current Godot compositor path.
Backdrop filter metadata flag indicating that the region uses a mask or blend mode unsupported by the current Godot compositor path.
Backdrop filter operation type for [code]blur()[/code]. Amount is CSS pixels before local view scaling.
Backdrop filter operation type for [code]brightness()[/code]. Amount is a multiplier where [code]1.0[/code] is unchanged.
Backdrop filter operation type for [code]contrast()[/code]. Amount is a multiplier where [code]1.0[/code] is unchanged.
Backdrop filter operation type for [code]saturate()[/code]. Amount is a multiplier where [code]1.0[/code] is unchanged.
Backdrop filter operation type for [code]grayscale()[/code]. Amount is a fraction where [code]0.0[/code] is unchanged and [code]1.0[/code] is fully applied.
Backdrop filter operation type for [code]sepia()[/code]. Amount is a fraction where [code]0.0[/code] is unchanged and [code]1.0[/code] is fully applied.
Backdrop filter operation type for [code]invert()[/code]. Amount is a fraction where [code]0.0[/code] is unchanged and [code]1.0[/code] is fully applied.
Backdrop filter operation type for [code]hue-rotate()[/code]. Amount is degrees.
Backdrop filter operation type for [code]opacity()[/code]. Amount is a multiplier where [code]1.0[/code] is unchanged.
